comment: I had Dr. Quintero for lab and he was really nice and a good professor that explained things really well. He did talk for a very long time before lab which most of the times wasn't needed, but he was very insightful and wanted us to do the best we could.

Dr. Quintero cares a lot about his students and really wants everyone to genuinely learn about biology and succeed, however his lectures are completely useless. The class itself is not difficult, but his tests are extremely specific and he grades questions subjectively. They also tend to ask questions that cover content he never discussed in class.

A lot of people aren't crazy about Dr. Quintero's teaching style, but those that buy into it absolutely love it/him. Dr. Quintero is genuinely one of the nicest people that I have met and I am fortunate to have had him as a professor. The level to which he cares about his students is unmatched.

Dr. Quintero was one of the best professors that I have ever had. He cares more about his students than he does himself and his ultimate goal is to get everyone to grow. If you're using these reviews to see if you should take his classes, I would recommend that you do

Dr. Quintero is a very kind professor who wants to see his students perform well. However, he tends to get sidetracked when questions are frequently asked during class, so I advise asking your questions after class. As long as you try your best, you will be fine. Go to office hours!

Dr. Q cares deeply about each of his students, and he truly wants everyone to succeed. That being said, his grading system is completely arbitrary and it kind of felt like he had already decided everyone's grades on day one. This class really improved my scientific paper reading skills, but I can't say I actually learned much about cell mechanics.

Omar is a genuine and caring professor who is always accessible, but he is clearly too smart to teach Bio 200. His obsession with guiding themes and long, drawn-out definitions of simple topics make test questions impossible, and his lectures are the most unorganized and meaningless that I have ever seen. Don't take without prev. bio knowledge.

Dr. Q is a really nice guy and clearly really smart, but he should not teach Bio200. His lectures focused so much on overarching themes and connections that he somehow managed to avoid teaching us any concrete information, which he tests us on anyway. His grading criteria was really unclear and much too picky considering his obsession with themes.

Best professor I had at UR, for both Bio 200 and 317. He was tough but helped me to grow and changed the way I understood science. Incredible office hours and passion to help his students succeed. If you put in the effort he will help you reach your full potential. His classes require effort but are the best that UR has to offer.

Such an incredible mentor and professor!!! I worked in his lab and it changed the way I view science. He has taught me so much about the scientific community, importance of collaboration, and how to critically think. He truly cares about each of his students. He goes out of his way to check on their well being and provide opportunities beyond UR.

Dr. Quintero is extremely nice and caring, but he is the most disorganized professor I've ever had. His lectures are confusing and he is not very good at explaining things in a way that make sense to most students. His exams are challenging and he assigns way too much homework. Overall, I would try to take a different professor if you can.

Dr. Quintero is an amazing professor. He cares about his students so much and will be there for you both in and outside of class. His course is extremely rigorous and will challenge you but you will be a better thinker and scientist because of it. You will not regret taking his course!!

The most unorganized professor I have ever had. His course outline made no sense and continued to unravel as the semester went on. He wants the students to develop critical thinking skills but provides no basis for the understanding of the papers he expects you to present and discuss. He is arrogant and unable to communicate what he expects. Avoid.

Dr. Quintero's style of teaching biology focuses more on understanding concepts rather than memorization. Personally, I thought this made classes much more interesting and easier to understand. He's a great professor and a great guy, I definitely recommend taking him for Bio 200

I love Dr Quintero! Not sure why the other comments are bad! He really connects with students & gets you to understand bio topics rather than memorize. He starts really broad (w/ context) and narrows in as we go, which I thought was really helpful. Very good at answering questions and in lab!! I love how he teaches and definitely recommend him!

Dr. Quintero is an amazing bio teacher, despite the other comments. He teaches bio in a new way that focuses more on the concepts and bio in general rather than root memorization, which is really helpful in the long run. He gives good feedback and if extremely receptive to comments. 10/10 would take again.

Dr. Quintero is a fun guy to talk to and is very helpful in lab and outside class. BUT, was a terrible lecture professor and wanted to discuss topics instead of teaching it first, which is very unhelpful. Not really sure how he wanted the answers to be written and did not really understand what he said int he questions.

He has a good personality and is super friendly. However, I can't get used to his way of teaching. Lectures are based on student discussion and answering questions. Grading scale is super vague. He also shows mild favoritism. I enjoy getting to know him, but I won't ever take his class again.
